headlines: MIAMI-DADE NOW ACCEPTS BITCOIN FOR PROPERTY TAX PAYMENTS
PAY YOUR MIAMI-DADE TAXES WITH BITCOIN
MIAMI-DADE MAKES HISTORY BY WELCOMING BITCOIN PROPERTY TAX PAYMENTS
draft.article: Miami-Dade property owners can now pay their property taxes using bitcoin. Tax Collector Dariel Fernandez announced Monday that taxpayers can use cryptocurrency online around the clock or in person across 13 county offices and T-Connect mobile units. A third-party vendor instantly converts every bitcoin transaction into U.S. dollars before the funds reach the county. Because of this conversion, Miami-Dade does not hold, invest in, or manage digital currency, while still receiving full dollar payments. The new option arrives during Florida's property tax collection season. Owners who submit payments by Nov. 30 receive a 4% early-payment discount under the county's Save the Max campaign before discounts decrease in December.

headlines: MIAMI CAROL CITY HIGH STUDENT ARRESTED WITH LOADED HANDGUN
STUDENT BRINGS LOADED GLOCK TO MIAMI GARDENS CAMPUS
INSTAGRAM PHOTO LEADS POLICE TO LOADED GUN AT SCHOOL
draft.article:
Miami-Dade Schools Police arrested 18-year-old student Torrez Ramon Thomas on Wednesday, Nov. 4, after he brought a loaded handgun to Miami Carol City Senior High School in Miami Gardens.

Authorities responded after the school principal received a tip about a social media post showing Thomas holding a firearm in a senior class Instagram group chat.

Officers searched the campus and located a turquoise-blue Sprayground backpack inside a classroom storage room. The bag held a black Glock 19 loaded with 15 rounds of ammunition, along with Thomas' Florida identification card.

Thomas later admitted to possessing the weapon, telling investigators he brought it for protection regarding a potential student fight.

headlines: MOTHER ARRESTED FOR CHILD ABUSE AT HIALEAH SUPERMARKET
HIALEAH MOM JAILED AFTER SUPERMARKET ATTACK
SURVEILLANCE VIDEO LEADS TO HIALEAH MOTHER ARREST ON PALM AVENUE
draft.article: Hialeah police arrested 43-year-old Madelien Nurrieta-Martinez after security cameras recorded her attacking her two young sons Wednesday night at a Palm Avenue supermarket. According to authorities, surveillance footage captured the mother pulling one child by both ears, grabbing the other boy by his hair, and biting his right ear. The violence continued outside the building, where she repeatedly struck both children. The market owner discovered the incident while checking camera footage the following day and contacted law enforcement. On Sunday afternoon, Nurrieta-Martinez appeared before Miami-Dade Circuit Court Judge Alicia Garcia Provolos, facing two felony counts of child abuse. Her bond was set at $5,000 with orders to stay away from the boys.

headlines: RECOUNT UNDERWAY IN MIAMI-DADE FOR DISTRICT 27 CONGRESSIONAL SEAT
1,100 VOTES DECIDE DISTRICT 27 RACE
CAN A DORAL RECOUNT FLIP FLORIDA DISTRICT 27?
draft.article: Election staff at the Miami-Dade Elections Headquarters in Doral are tallying nearly 250,000 ballots in the contested race for Florida's 27th Congressional District. Miami-Dade County Supervisor of Elections Alina Garcia expects the machine recount to conclude Tuesday afternoon. Incumbent Republican Maria Elvira Salazar holds a narrow 1,100-vote lead over Democratic challenger Eliott Rodriguez. Under state law, an automatic recount occurs when the margin is within a half-percentage point. Workers processed ballots continuously overnight, completing Election Day and mail-in votes before advancing to early ballots. The count went forward after federal judge David S. Leibowitz rejected an emergency request from Rodriguez's campaign to remove Garcia from the canvassing board.

Located at 190, 198, and 210 Palm Avenue, the more than two-acre site spans roughly 300 feet along Biscayne Bay with sweeping views of the Miami skyline. Owner Jorge Luis Garcia previously offered the three existing Mediterranean-style mansions for $150 million. The new listing includes plans by Miami-based Choeff Levy Fischman Architecture and Design to replace the residences with a 30,000-square-foot tropical estate. The proposed build includes ten bedrooms, a car museum with turntables, and a 1,950-square-foot infinity pool. A sale at full price would break Miami-Dade County's residential sales record set on Indian Creek Island.

headlines: JUDGE RULES ALINA GARCIA WILL OVERSEE MIAMI-DADE RECOUNT
MIAMI-DADE ELECTIONS CHIEF WINS COURT BATTLE
WHY A FEDERAL JUDGE REFUSED TO STOP THIS RECOUNT
draft.article: Miami-Dade County Supervisor of Elections Alina Garcia will continue directing the machine recount for Florida's 27th Congressional District after a federal judge dismissed a challenge against her. U.S. District Judge David Leibowitz rejected a motion from Democratic candidate Eliott Rodriguez, who sought to disqualify Garcia over alleged bias toward incumbent Republican Representative María Elvira Salazar. The local race is separated by only 1,090 votes, or 0.44 percentage points. Rodriguez cited Garcia's post-election remarks, social media posts, and her son-in-law's legal representation of Salazar. Leibowitz deemed Garcia's victory comments improper, but ruled they did not warrant her removal from the ongoing recount.

headlines: INTER MIAMI HOSTS ANNUAL MEDIA APPRECIATION DAY AT NU STADIUM
NU STADIUM HOSTS MEDIA SOCCER TOURNAMENT
MIAMI JOURNALISTS COMPETE ON INTER MIAMIS NEW HOME PITCH
draft.article:
On Sunday, Inter Miami CF opened Nu Stadium to local and international journalists for the 2026 Media Appreciation Day and Copa de Medios tournament. It marked the first time the signature event took place inside the club's new Miami home.

Before tournament play kicked off on the pitch, the club paid tribute to Miami Herald sports reporter Michelle Kaufman for her thirty-year career. Four media squads then competed, with Team Presagio defeating Team Euforia in the final.

About 60 children participated in the inaugural Copita de Medios clinic led by academy coaches. Guests also toured the player tunnel, the Leo Messi Stand, and viewed club trophies including the 2025 MLS Cup.

OUR CITY WELCOMES NBA ALL-STAR GAME BACK AFTER DECADES
draft.article: Miami is set to host the 2028 NBA All-Star Weekend from February 18 to February 20 at Kaseya Center. This marks only the second time our city will host the annual showcase and the first time since 1990. NBA Commissioner Adam Silver is scheduled to visit South Florida next month for the formal league announcement. Festivities will span several South Florida venues, including the All-Star Celebrity Game on Friday night, the Rising Stars Challenge, and Saturday's dunk and 3-point contests. Miami Heat players are already anticipating the massive event. Team captain Bam Adebayo praised the city's loud culture and warm weather, while guard Davion Mitchell noted that basketball fans will flock to South Florida for an energetic weekend.
